none: PAS NLM-F594B5: Roman ToT Ring from Kirton in Lindsey
contea di ritrovamento: Lincolnshire (Inghilterra e Galles)

A Roman silver finger-ring with a broad rectangular bezel and triangular shoulders. Simple incised lines emphasize the borders and 'frame' the bezel, within which the letters ToT are engraved, the T's with neatly-formed seriphs. There are signs of wear, most notably on the bezel and at the rear of the hoop. Rings with 'ToT' inscriptions are distinctively Romano-British and concentrated in Lincolnshire. The inscription is regarded as an abbreviation of the Celtic god-name Toutatis/ Totatis, a deity who was often conflated with the Roman god Mars (M. Henig and J. Ogden, Antiquaries Journal 67, 1987, 366-7; A. Daubney, 'The cult of Totatis: evidence for tribal identity in mid Roman Britain',…
